stage11Disposition.sharedVocabularyWithoutSharedAuthority: PARTIAL: M300 preserves distinct local-project, repository, and active-GM authority for four adapters; M308 and M337 preserve project identity, hashes, and human/no-provider review, but content-bearing project and asset payload boundaries remain producer-specific.

sharedFindings: M319's eleven-family map remains accurate after M320-M337; M337 closes only the packaged rename-review input boundary and does not alter producer ownership.
The generic core, adapters, project session, and review surface preserve separate review and target authority; approval does not itself confer native project-store authority.
Ordinary create/save/save-as remain content-bearing and must keep atomic persistence, backup, generation, asset-tree, directory-entry, and foreign-state semantics outside generic history payloads.
Asset import/binding and recovery restore/detach retain role-specific bytes and authority outside generic ProposalBatch history until a separately accepted boundary exists.
M303 is the direct local apply/undo/reread proof; M337 is a packaged review/cancel proof. Neither alone certifies the full Stage 11 every-producer acceptance observation.

selectedNextSlice.name: test-owned metadata-only project-rename execution, undo, and authoritative reread
selectedNextSlice.scope: Implement one exact project-store executor for the existing approved metadata-only project.rename batch on a fresh disposable test-owned project, with explicit approval, authoritative reread, inverse rename undo, append-only receipts, and exact project/workspace/foreign-state preservation. Keep create/save/save-as content payloads, asset bytes, provider, credentials, Foundry, and player passwords outside the slice.
selectedNextSlice.reason: M337 proves the review boundary but not execution. Completing one existing content-independent producer end to end is the smallest direct gap toward the Stage 11 live acceptance without inventing a generic raw-content envelope.
